articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities, Issues New General Licenses, and Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC issued Iran General License GG, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving 'Karnakis and Karnakis,' and Iran General License HH, which permits wind down activities, limited safety and environmental transactions, and the offloading of cargo involving certain persons or vessels blocked on October 21, 2026.

In addition to the Iran-related actions, OFAC also announced the removal of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea. The specific entities or individuals removed from these sanctions lists were not detailed in the initial announcement but are reflected in updates to the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

Furthermore, OFAC issued Russia-related General License 131K, authorizing certain transactions for the negotiation of and entry into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH and related maintenance activities. Two amended Frequently Asked Questions, FAQ 1224 and FAQ 1225, were also released to provide further guidance.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations Targeting Chinese Entities and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) on October 19, 2026. These designations targeted five entities located in Beijing and Shanghai, China, adding them to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List (NS-MBS List).

The designated entities include Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (also known as Miracle Plus RMB Fund I), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase II Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (also known as Miracle Plus RMB Fund II), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Zhiyuan Enterprise Management Center Limited Partnership, Qiji Chuangtan Beijing Investment Management Co Ltd (also known as MiraclePlus), and Shanghai Zhisuan Technology Co Ltd.

Each designation under PAIPA Section 2 includes measures such as the blocking of property, restrictions on loans from U.S. financial institutions, prohibitions on foreign exchange and banking transactions, and a ban on U.S. persons investing in or purchasing significant amounts of the entity's equity or debt. OFAC also issued PAIPA General License 1, authorizing transactions pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations, and PAIPA General License 2, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving certain entities blocked on October 19, 2026.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Venezuela-related General License 60A on October 16, 2026, titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela.' This amended general license replaces and supersedes the previous General License 60.

General License 60A extends the authorization period for earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela from its original expiration date of October 23, 2026, to April 21, 2027. This extension aims to ensure continued support for humanitarian aid in the region.
In conjunction with the amended general license, OFAC also issued an updated Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, to provide further clarification and guidance regarding the authorized transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian Entities and Cuban Bank, Issues New General Licenses Under 'Operation Economic Outcast'
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation on October 15, 2026, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' an ongoing campaign targeting Iran's financial networks. The sanctions target a range of banks, exchange houses, companies, and individuals involved in Iran's financial and petroleum sectors.

Among the principal targets is Iraq-based International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (IDB), designated for operating in the financial sector of the Iranian economy and providing financial facilitation services and U.S. dollar access for Iran. The action also targets Sayyed Ruhollah Razavi, described as an oil intermediary involved in selling Iranian oil and repatriating revenue.

In a coordinated action, the U.S. Department of State designated Cuba-based Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) for providing services to the sanctioned Iran-based Karafarin Bank since at least 2022. OFAC also issued Iran-related General License FF, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving IDB, and new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions related to Russia and Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez from Venezuela Sanctions List
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the removal of Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List on October 14, 2026. This action lifts the associated asset freeze and removes obstacles for U.S. persons attempting to deal with him.

Rodriguez Gomez, who has served as the President of Venezuela's National Assembly since 2021 and previously as vice president under Hugo Chavez, was initially designated in 2018. His designation was part of broader sanctions targeting members of Nicolas Maduro's inner circle.
The removal of Rodriguez Gomez from the SDN list signifies a change in his sanctioned status under the Venezuela sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities Linked to Mexican Cartel and Terrorism Networks
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism designations on October 13, 2026. These actions target individuals and entities associated with illicit drug trafficking and terrorism.

Among the individuals added to OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List are Gamaliel Garza Elias and Gamaliel Garza Garcia, both with ties to Anahuac, Nuevo Leon, Mexico, and linked to the Cartel del Noreste. Also designated was Pablo Cesar Guajardo Alvarez, known as 'El Takia,' from Tamaulipas, Mexico.

Entities designated include Club La Molienda, Cuadra San Diban, Distribuidora de Gas Economico, S.A. de C.V., and Gas Energia Confiable, S.A. de C.V., all located in Mexico and identified as facilitators for the Cartel del Noreste. These designations underscore the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to disrupt the financial and operational networks of transnational criminal organizations.

articles.headline: Bank of America Settles with OFAC for $11.6 Million Over Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an $11,662,930 settlement with Bank of America, N.A. on October 13, 2026. The settlement resolves Bank of America's potential civil liability for 475 apparent violations of multiple OFAC sanctions programs.

The apparent violations involved transactions related to sanctions programs targeting Russia, Belarus, Iran, Burma, Somalia, narcotics, and global terrorism. These violations occurred due to the bank processing payments involving blocked banks, failing to prioritize alerts for exact name and date of birth matches to blocked persons, not promptly updating watchlists, and mishandling business accounts associated with blocked persons.

OFAC determined that Bank of America's apparent violations were non-egregious and largely not voluntarily self-disclosed. The settlement amount reflects no reduction to the base penalty, including no mitigation for remedial measures or cooperation, and includes significant compliance commitments from the bank.

articles.headline: OFAC Settles with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Designates International Criminal Court, and Removes Burma Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026, for $175,015. The freight forwarding firm settled its potential civil liability for four apparent violations of the Illicit Drug Trafficking Sanctions Regulations and six apparent violations of the Reporting, Procedures and Penalties Regulations.

Between September 2023 and February 2024, Pegasus dealt in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company and failed to respond fully to an OFAC subpoena for six months. OFAC determined the conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed.

Concurrently, OFAC designated the entire International Criminal Court (ICC) under Executive Order 14203 and issued four related General Licenses (GLs 13-16) authorizing specific transactions involving the court. Additionally, OFAC announced a Burma-related designation removal, updating its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License for Diesel Fuel Transactions
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Russia-related General License 135 on October 9, 2026. This new general license is titled 'Authorizing Transactions Related to the Sale, Delivery, Offloading, and Importation of Diesel Fuel of Russian Federation Origin.'
This action by OFAC aims to provide specific authorization for certain transactions involving Russian diesel fuel, potentially to address market stability or supply chain considerations.
The issuance of General License 135 indicates a targeted approach to managing the impact of sanctions on specific commodities while maintaining broader restrictions on the Russian Federation.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations and Issues New General Licenses for Iran and Russia
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 8, 2026. These designations are part of ongoing efforts to target entities and individuals supporting the Iranian regime.
In conjunction with the new designations, OFAC issued an Iran-related General License, the details of which were not immediately specified but are intended to authorize certain transactions.

Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Russia-related General License, further adjusting the scope of authorized activities under the Russia sanctions program. These actions reflect OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions implementation and adjustment.

articles.headline: Bank of America Fined Over $11.6 Million by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: Bank of America, N.A. has agreed to pay a civil penalty of $11,662,930 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This settlement addresses 475 apparent violations of multiple OFAC sanctions programs.

The violations involved processing payments through blocked banks, failing to properly screen customers against sanctions lists, and mishandling accounts associated with sanctioned individuals. These failures exposed the U.S. financial system to illicit finance risks.
The penalty reflects OFAC's determination that the violations were non-egregious but largely not voluntarily self-disclosed, with no reduction for remedial measures or cooperation.

articles.headline: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics Settles with OFAC for $175,015 in Sanctions Case
body: Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, a California-based freight forwarding firm, has agreed to remit $175,015 to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of U.S. sanctions. The settlement was announced by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).

The violations included dealing in blocked property by facilitating the importation of a machine supplied by a designated company and failing to fully respond to an OFAC subpoena. These actions highlight the importance of robust sanctions compliance programs for logistics companies.
OFAC determined that Pegasus's conduct was non-egregious and not voluntarily disclosed, leading to the imposition of the civil penalty.

articles.headline: Individual Fined Over $1.4 Million by OFAC for Sanctions Violations
body: An individual has been assessed a civil penalty of $1,427,230 by the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) for apparent violations of sanctions regulations. The details of the specific violations were not immediately released but typically involve unauthorized transactions with sanctioned entities or jurisdictions.
This significant penalty underscores OFAC's commitment to enforcing sanctions against individuals who engage in prohibited activities, regardless of their affiliation with larger organizations.
The action serves as a reminder that individuals are directly accountable for compliance with U.S. sanctions laws and regulations, and that violations can result in substantial financial penalties.

articles.headline: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. Pays $60,764 for Sanctions Violations
body: Rice Lake Weighing Systems, Inc. has agreed to pay $60,764 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) to settle its potential civil liability for apparent violations of sanctions regulations. The specific nature of the violations was not detailed in the public announcement.
This enforcement action highlights the importance of comprehensive sanctions compliance programs for companies involved in international trade, even for seemingly routine business operations.
The settlement amount reflects OFAC's assessment of the violations, taking into account various factors such as the company's cooperation and remedial measures taken to prevent future occurrences.

articles.headline: Federal Reserve Signals Continued Vigilance on Inflation Amidst Mixed Economic Data
body: Federal Reserve officials have indicated a continued hawkish stance on monetary policy, emphasizing the need for sustained vigilance against inflation despite recent mixed economic indicators. Recent statements from various Fed governors suggest that while inflation has shown signs of moderating, it remains above the central bank's target, necessitating a cautious approach to interest rate adjustments.

Market analysts are closely watching upcoming inflation reports and employment figures for further clues on the Fed's next moves. The consensus among economists points to a potential pause in rate hikes in the near term, but the possibility of further tightening remains on the table if inflationary pressures resurface.

The Fed's dual mandate of maximizing employment and maintaining price stability continues to guide its decisions, with policymakers balancing the risks of overtightening against the dangers of entrenched inflation. The current economic environment presents a complex challenge, requiring careful calibration of monetary tools.

articles.headline: Global Oil Prices Surge on Geopolitical Tensions and Supply Concerns
body: Global oil prices experienced a significant surge this week, driven by escalating geopolitical tensions in key producing regions and renewed concerns over crude oil supply. Brent crude futures rose above $95 per barrel, while WTI futures also saw substantial gains, reflecting heightened market anxiety.

Analysts attribute the price hike to a combination of factors, including ongoing conflicts that threaten oil transit routes and recent production cuts by major oil-exporting nations. The market is also reacting to stronger-than-expected demand forecasts for the upcoming winter season.

The sustained increase in energy costs is expected to put upward pressure on inflation globally, potentially complicating efforts by central banks to manage price stability. Governments are closely monitoring the situation, with some considering strategic reserve releases to temper price volatility.

articles.headline: EU and UK Reach Provisional Agreement on Post-Brexit Trade Dispute
body: The European Union and the United Kingdom have reached a provisional agreement aimed at resolving a long-standing trade dispute stemming from post-Brexit arrangements. The breakthrough follows intensive negotiations and is expected to ease trade friction and improve economic relations between the two blocs.

The agreement reportedly addresses key areas of contention, including customs procedures and regulatory alignment for certain goods. While details are still emerging, both sides have expressed optimism that the deal will foster greater stability and predictability for businesses operating across the English Channel.

The resolution of this trade dispute is anticipated to provide a much-needed boost to economic confidence in both the EU and the UK, potentially leading to increased investment and trade flows in the coming months.

articles.headline: Humanitarian Crisis Deepens in Gaza Amidst Ongoing Conflict
body: The humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip has significantly worsened this week, with international aid organizations reporting severe shortages of food, water, and medical supplies. Ongoing conflict and restrictions on aid access have exacerbated the dire situation for the civilian population.

Hospitals are struggling to cope with the influx of casualties and a critical lack of resources, leading to widespread concerns about public health. Calls for a sustained humanitarian ceasefire and unimpeded access for aid convoys have intensified from global bodies and numerous countries.

Diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the conflict and establish humanitarian corridors continue, but progress remains elusive. The international community is urging all parties to prioritize the protection of civilians and adhere to international humanitarian law.

articles.headline: Sudan Peace Talks Resume with International Mediation Efforts
body: Peace talks aimed at resolving the ongoing conflict in Sudan have resumed this week, with international mediators facilitating discussions between the warring factions. The renewed diplomatic push seeks to establish a lasting ceasefire and pave the way for a political transition.

Representatives from various regional and international bodies are participating in the negotiations, emphasizing the urgent need to end the violence and address the humanitarian crisis gripping the country. Previous attempts at brokering peace have faced significant challenges, but there is renewed hope for progress.

The talks are focusing on key issues such as power-sharing arrangements, security sector reform, and the protection of civilians. The international community has pledged support for a comprehensive peace agreement and its implementation.

articles.headline: ASEAN Leaders Call for Renewed Dialogue in Myanmar
body: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have issued a joint statement calling for renewed dialogue and a peaceful resolution to the political crisis in Myanmar. The statement, released after a regional summit, reiterated concerns over the humanitarian situation and the lack of progress in implementing the ASEAN Five-Point Consensus.

The regional bloc urged all parties in Myanmar to engage in constructive dialogue to find a durable solution that reflects the will of the people. Special envoys have been appointed to facilitate discussions and encourage a return to democratic processes.

While direct intervention remains off the table, ASEAN continues to play a crucial role in regional diplomacy, seeking to exert pressure for a peaceful transition and the protection of human rights in Myanmar.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Significant Enforcement Actions Against Major Banks for BSA/AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a series of enforcement actions for October 2026, including significant civil money penalties against major financial institutions for deficiencies in their Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) compliance programs.

American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah, received a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million civil money penalty for BSA compliance program deficiencies, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence and customer identification program violations.

Bank of America, National Association, Charlotte, North Carolina, was assessed a $750 million civil money penalty for similar deficiencies in its BSA/AML compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and sending wires with inaccurate transmittor name information. These actions underscore the OCC's commitment to holding banks accountable for robust compliance frameworks.

articles.headline: OCC Issues Prohibition Orders Against Bank Employees for Embezzlement
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued prohibition orders against two institution-affiliated parties (IAPs) in October 2026 for embezzling customer funds. These actions reinforce the accountability of individuals for their conduct within financial institutions.
Jennifer Hamblin, a Vault Teller at a Cincinnati, Ohio, branch of Fifth Third Bank, N.A., was issued an Order of Prohibition for embezzling approximately $292,000 in customer funds.

Similarly, Christopher Organista, a Former Operations Processor at the La Mirada, California Operations Center of U.S. Bank National Association, received an Order of Prohibition for embezzling approximately $194,131 in bank customer funds. These orders prohibit the individuals from any further participation in the affairs of a bank or other financial institution.

articles.headline: OCC Announces Enforcement Actions for October 2026
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today released enforcement actions for October 2026.

articles.headline: OCC Imposes $750 Million Assessment Against Bank of America for Deficient BSA/AML Compliance
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a $750 million civil money penalty against Bank of America, N.A. (bank), for violations of the Bank Secrecy Act and its implementing regulations, including 12 CFR 21.21 and 12 CFR 21.11. This amount is the largest in OCC history.

articles.headline: OCC Assesses $350 Million Civil Money Penalty Against American Express
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah (bank), for deficiencies in the bank's Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

articles.headline: BIS Publishes Final Rule Amending Export Administration Regulations for Emerging Technologies
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has published a final rule in the Federal Register amending the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to impose new controls on certain emerging technologies. This action is part of the U.S. government's ongoing strategy to safeguard national security interests and prevent sensitive technologies from falling into the wrong hands.

The amendments specifically target technologies with potential dual-use applications, which could be critical for both civilian and military purposes. The rule clarifies licensing requirements and expands the scope of items subject to export restrictions, particularly for destinations of concern.

Industry stakeholders are advised to review the updated regulations carefully to ensure compliance with the new export control measures. BIS emphasized its commitment to working with the private sector to navigate these changes and maintain a strong export control system.

articles.headline: BIS Adds Chinese Technology Firms to Entity List Over National Security Concerns
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has added several Chinese technology firms to its Entity List, citing national security concerns. This action restricts the export, reexport, and in-country transfer of certain U.S. technologies to these designated entities without a license.

The listed companies are primarily involved in advanced computing, artificial intelligence, and surveillance technologies, areas identified by the U.S. government as critical for maintaining technological leadership and preventing misuse by foreign adversaries.

This move signals a continued effort by the U.S. to curb China's access to advanced technologies that could support its military modernization or human rights abuses. Companies engaging with these entities will face increased scrutiny and stringent licensing requirements.

articles.headline: Revisions to the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) revises the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing two addresses associated with Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. from the Entity List under the destination of China, People's Republic of (China). This determination follows the removal from the Entity List of Arrow China Electronics Trading Co., Ltd., and the removal of six aliases for Arrow Electronics (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. in November 2025.

articles.headline: Removal From the Entity List
body: In this rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) by removing one entity from the Entity List under the destination of Turkey.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
